newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end weaker, snap record streak.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end weaker, snap record streak.

text.p: Toronto stocks finished softer on Monday, ending a record-setting five-session rally as nervous investors turned their attention to the Federal Reserve's key policy meeting on Tuesday.
The TSE 300 Composite Index slipped 3.21 points to close at 5284.26 in modest turnover of 55.2 million shares worth C$704 million ($515 million).
Declining stocks outnumbered advancers 507 to 373, with 310 issues unchanged.
"Essentially, it's been a nothing day. Light trading and no real direction," said John Kellett, vice-president of equities at Royal Bank of Canada.
Financial markets have already discounted a rate increase of 25 basis points by the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee following its meeting tomorrow, Kellett said.
"I would suspect if they didn't increase rates, then the market may be mildly disappointed. It just means it's later than sooner," he said.
Toronto suffered losses in nine of 14 sub-groups.
Communications, gold and base metals led the decline, while the strong side included technology and banking stocks.
The TSE closed at record highs in five consecutive sessions last week.
* Gulfstream Resources Canada Ltd. topped the most-active list, rising 0.20 to 8.70 on 1.2 million shares. Canadian 88 Energy Corp also improved 0.20 to 5.35.
* Takeover target Loewen Group Inc. fell 0.90 to 56.50. The Canadian funeral home operator is expected to respond this week to a hostile bid from rival Service Corp International.
* Bank stocks were also heavy traders. Toronto-Dominion Bank rose 0.20 to 29, a 52-week high, on 1.1 million shares.
Bank of Montreal eased 0.05 to 36.55 on 893,000 shares.
* The top gainer was Fairfax Financial Holdings Ltd., up 4 to 259.
